title: Meal-prep cook card (v3 — self-contained recipes)
description: v3.0.0. Each Recipe is FULLY SELF-CONTAINED: its own two-phase cook plan, per-ingredient macro breakdown, reheat, and a RELATIVE prep schedule all live inside it — so any recipe (including one pulled from a past week) renders and re-cooks in isolation. The two phases are NAMED OBJECTS, not a list: `misePhase` (bowls + standalones — do-ahead prep, frequently done the day before) and `cookPhase` (an ordered steps[] whose backgroundable kickoff step(s) lead, so the app surfaces the long hands-off task first and the user can start it and move on while it runs). 'Background' is now a per-step flag (CookStep.backgroundable), NOT a phase — the old Phase-0/1/2 array collapsed to these two named phases. There is NO author-time shared-mise consolidation: every ingredient carries a CANONICAL IDENTITY (ingredientId + canonical unit + preparation + combinable) so the CLIENT combines overlapping MISE across an arbitrary user-selected set of recipes at cook time (or in one day-before chopping pass). One unified Ingredient shape is used by both mise bowls and cook steps. Removed/relocated from v2: cookPlan wrapper + phases array + Phase-0/1/2 ordinals, containerMath, reheatReference, macroReconciliation, top-level schedule, shared-mise consolidation (sharedMise/isShared/sharedId), weekOverview, leftovers, substitutions, week-shopping logistics (pickupDate/firstMealDate/household), and per-step/bowl ordinal numbers (array position is the order). Top level is just meta + recipes[]. Daily macro totals are DERIVED by the consumer (Σ recipes' perServing); recipe.perServing is itself the Σ of its macroBreakdown rows.

uploadedAt.description: Server-resolved Firestore timestamp injected by upload.py; absent in on-disk JSON.

Macro.$comment: No additionalProperties:false — base of allOf extensions (macro rows add name/amount).

cookDate.description: Historical anchor — the week this card was authored for. A re-cook of a single recipe schedules its own prep from Recipe.prepSchedule relative offsets.

emoji.description: Self-contained on the recipe (no top-level emojiLegend in v3).

perServing.description: DERIVED = exact sum of macroBreakdown.ingredients[] rows. derive.py sets it; never hand-authored.

activeMinutes.description: The single home for active cook minutes (no duplicate on the phases).

PrepStep.description: Per-recipe prep in RELATIVE time so it re-schedules against any future cook date. The client may merge identical combinable prep across a multi-recipe selection. Distinct from misePhase: this is fixed-offset, days/hours-ahead work (marinade, thaw); misePhase is flexible-timing chopping the user can do anytime up to (and often the day before) the cook.

combinable.description: Default true. False for prep that can't be pooled across recipes.

MisePhase.description: Phase 1 of 2 — do-ahead prep: `bowls` + `standalones`, NO cook steps. Frequently done the day before cooking; the client may combine mise across multiple user-selected recipes into one chopping pass (canonical ingredientId merge). The display title is a client-side constant ('Mise'), not stored. No holdsOvernight flag — the user decides what to prep ahead vs day-of.

description.description: Optional recipe-specific note (e.g. 'salsa is better made the night before').

CookPhase.description: Phase 2 of 2 — cook-day actions as an ordered `steps[]`, NO mise bowls. The backgroundable kickoff step(s) lead (CookStep.backgroundable=true) so the app surfaces the long hands-off task first — start it, then move on to another recipe while it runs. Active cook + portion steps follow. The display title is a client-side constant ('Cook'), not stored.

description.description: Optional recipe-specific note about the cook session.

MiseBowl.description: A grouped mise bowl. Its `ingredients` carry canonical identity so the CLIENT can combine this bowl with same-ingredient+same-prep ingredients from OTHER selected recipes. Position in bowls[] is the order (no bowlNumber).

steps.description: Prose prep actions for this bowl (e.g. 'Combine in one bowl; toss').

Ingredient.description: The ONE ingredient shape, used by both mise bowls and cook steps. The CLIENT merges MISE ingredients across recipes by (ingredientId, unit, preparation): same id + same unit + same prep sum into one combined bowl; differing prep stays separate. Cook-step ingredients carry the same shape for cross-reference but are not merged.

ingredientId.description: Stable canonical slug, e.g. 'white-rice', 'lime', 'yellow-onion'. Merge key.

quantity.description: Number for mergeable mise; may be a display string (e.g. '~135') on cook steps.

unit.description: Canonical unit: g, ml, each, clove, tsp, Tbsp, wedge, pinch, can, …

preparation.description: e.g. 'diced', 'sliced', 'juiced'. Part of the mise merge key — different prep can't share a bowl.

combinable.description: Mise only. Default true; false for 'to taste' / pinch / pan-oil items.

MiseStandalone.description: An item that needs no prep bowl (stays in its own container) but should appear in the mise list.

CookStep.description: An ordered cook-day step: prose `steps` plus any structured `ingredients` it acts on (same Ingredient shape as mise — but cook ingredients are NOT combined across recipes). The first step(s) are typically backgroundable (long + hands-off) and lead the cookPhase. Self-contained: no cross-recipe references. Position in steps[] is the order (no stepNumber).

backgroundable.description: Default false. True = long-running + hands-off (start it and walk away — rice, sous-vide, oven roast). The app surfaces backgroundable steps first and lets the user move to another recipe while the timer runs; these lead the cookPhase. Pairs with `timer`.

handsOff.description: Concurrent hands-off ops in THIS recipe (plain strings — no cross-recipe references).

MacroBreakdown.description: Canonical per-serving macro source. recipe.perServing = the exact Σ of these rows (derive.py). The app can also display the breakdown and sum any subset.

allOf.description: Per-serving macro row: the 4 macros plus the ingredient name and per-serving amount (quantity/unit inlined — no nested Amount object).

displayHint.description: Free text when not a clean number, e.g. 'from ~180g raw', 'trace', '¼ avocado'.
